intro: The causative (-せる / -させる) adds a new person at the top of the sentence: the one who makes or lets someone act. The causer is the subject (は / が). The person made to act drops to を or に, and which one depends on the verb. Turn the causative into a passive (-させられる) and the person made to act becomes the subject again, with the causer marked に.

skills.rule: If the verb already has a を object, the person made to act takes に; with a verb that has no object, を means "make" and に means "let".
skills.explain:
Transitive verb with its own object: the causee is always に, because Japanese avoids two を on one verb. 母は弟に野菜を食べさせた "Mum made my brother eat his vegetables". The same holds when the object is only understood: 私に払わせてください "let me pay".

Verb with no object (行く, 来る, 帰る, 走る, 休む): both are possible, and they differ. を means the causee had no say: 子供を早く帰らせた "made the children go home early". に respects their wish: 子供に好きなだけ遊ばせた "let the children play as much as they liked". If the verb takes a path with を (公園を走る), the causee must be に.

Verbs of emotion and reaction (泣く, 笑う, 怒る, 驚く, 心配する, 喜ぶ) take only を: 母を心配させた. 待たせる also takes を for the person: 友達を待たせた, お待たせしました.
patterns: [causer] は [causee] に [object] を [verb-(さ)せる]
[person] を [泣かせる / 心配させる / 待たせる]

examples.jp: 私[わたし]{に}払[はら]わせてください。
先生[せんせい]は学生[がくせい]{に}本[ほん]を読[よ]ませました。
examples.en: The teacher had the students read the book.

examples.jp: 母[はは]は弟[おとうと]{に}野菜[やさい]を食[た]べさせました。
examples.en: Mum made my little brother eat his vegetables.

examples.jp: 遅[おく]れて、友達[ともだち]{を}一時間[いちじかん]も待[ま]たせてしまいました。
examples.en: I was late and kept my friend waiting a whole hour.

examples.jp: 子供[こども]{を}泣[な]かせてはいけません。
父[ちち]は熱[ねつ]がある妹[いもうと]{を}学校[がっこう]に行[い]かせませんでした。
examples.en: My father didn't send my sister to school when she had a fever.

contrast.note: を for the causee only when the verb has no object of its own. With an object present (野菜を), the causee must move to に.
が (or は) marks the causer, the one who makes or lets. The person made to act is never が in an active causative.
と means "together with". 弟と食べさせた would mean someone ate along with your brother, not that he was made to eat.

mistakes.bad: 母[はは]は弟[おとうと]を野菜[やさい]を食[た]べさせました。
mistakes.good: 母[はは]は弟[おとうと]{に}野菜[やさい]を食[た]べさせました。
mistakes.note: Two を on one verb is not allowed. The object keeps を, so the person eating takes に.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]が払[はら]わせてください。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]{に}払[はら]わせてください。
mistakes.note: You are the one allowed to pay, not the one giving permission. The causee is に.

mistakes.bad: 彼女[かのじょ]に泣[な]かせてしまいました。
mistakes.good: 彼女[かのじょ]{を}泣[な]かせてしまいました。
mistakes.note: Emotional reactions like crying take を for the person you caused it in.

skills.tip: Count the を. Is there already one on the verb? Causee gets に. None? Forced, or an emotion: を. Allowed: に.

skills.rule: In a causative-passive (-させられる) the person made to act is the subject, and the one who made them takes に: 私は母に野菜を食べさせられた.
skills.explain:
Start from the causative 母が私に野菜を食べさせた "Mum made me eat vegetables". Make it passive and you, the one forced, become the subject; Mum drops to に: 私は母に野菜を食べさせられた "I was made to eat vegetables by Mum". Anything you were made to do something to keeps を.

The form says you did it against your will. Ichidan verbs take -させられる (食べさせられる). Godan verbs usually shorten to -される: 待たされる, 飲まされる, 歌わされる, 走らされる. Verbs ending in す cannot shorten: 話させられる, not 話さされる. する becomes させられる, 来る becomes 来させられる.

Do not confuse it with the plain causative, where the causer is the subject: 母は私に… vs 私は母に…させられた. In both, に sits on a person, but a different one. In the causative-passive, に is always the one who did the forcing.
patterns: [person forced] は [causer] に [object] を [verb-させられる / -される]
[causer] に [待たされる / 飲まされる / 歌わされる]

examples.jp: 部長[ぶちょう]{に}お酒[さけ]を飲[の]まされました。
駅[えき]で友達[ともだち]{に}一時間[いちじかん]も待[ま]たされました。
examples.en: My friend kept me waiting at the station for a whole hour.

examples.jp: 子供[こども]のころ、母[はは]{に}ピアノを習[なら]わされました。
examples.en: When I was a child, my mother made me take piano lessons.

examples.jp: 先生[せんせい]{に}作文[さくぶん]を書[か]き直[なお]させられました。
examples.en: The teacher made me rewrite my essay.

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]コーチ{に}グラウンドを十周[じゅっしゅう]走[はし]らされます。
examples.en: Every day the coach makes us run ten laps of the field.

contrast.note: を stays on what you were made to act on (お酒を, ピアノを). The person who forced you is never を.
が (or は) marks you, the one who was made to act. The causer cannot be が in this form.
The causer of a causative-passive is marked に. から is not the normal choice here.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]は母[はは]を野菜[やさい]を食[た]べさせられました。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]は母[はは]{に}野菜[やさい]を食[た]べさせられました。
mistakes.note: Mum did the forcing, so she is に. を stays only on the vegetables.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]は先生[せんせい]が作文[さくぶん]を書[か]かされました。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]は先生[せんせい]{に}作文[さくぶん]を書[か]かされました。
mistakes.note: One subject only: the person forced. The one who made you do it takes に.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]で友達[ともだち]で一時間[いちじかん]も待[ま]たされました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]で友達[ともだち]{に}一時間[いちじかん]も待[ま]たされました。
mistakes.note: で marks the place (駅で). The person who kept you waiting is に.

skills.tip: Hear -させられる or -される with a sigh in it? Ask "who made me?" That person gets に.
